title: Prohibit agent-authored Git commits
objective: Record and enforce the repository-owner rule that AI agents may inspect Git, prepare changes, create isolated branches, and assist with pull requests, but must never create a Git commit or cause an implicit commit; only humans commit, and the default branch is never an agent write target.
validations: Root AGENTS, master DEC-053, accepted ADR-0015, coordination protocol, policy registry, and current planning all prohibit agent-authored commits on every branch
node --test tools/scripts/agent-task-guard.test.mjs: 14/14 guard contracts passed, including direct/implicit commit denial, default-branch denial, isolated branch allowance, and ff-only pull
Claude's tracked PreToolUse configuration invokes the provider-neutral guard and now identifies both task ownership and Git policy
CI executes the guard contract suite before TypeScript behavior contracts
pnpm.cmd docs:check passed after regenerating derived Graph IR and artifact evidence
pnpm.cmd ai:check passed for 26 task records and pnpm.cmd ai:audit passed with zero model calls or side effects
risks: A repository Git hook would also block normal human commits, so enforcement must remain in agent policy/adapters rather than a global pre-commit hook.
Shell command parsing is defense in depth and cannot replace canonical agent compliance for providers without a runtime adapter.
Pull-request assistance is allowed only around branches containing human-authored commits; agents cannot manufacture a PR by committing themselves.
